text:
Priya (PM): Quick sync: a few enterprise customers asked for a way to 'lock' audit evidence for legal / compliance without changing tenant retention settings. Need to define MVP and non-goals.

Evan (Eng): Two technical patterns: 1) a tenant-scoped pin flag on existing objects (fast) 2) export-to-archive with tamper-evident manifest + optional immutability (stronger).

Nina (Security): From SOC2 perspective, we prefer export + signed manifest. Metadata should include signer id, timestamp, export hash chain. Pin-by-flag is acceptable as interim for low-risk cases.

Carlos (Legal): Requirements: export must be human- and machine-readable, include chain-of-custody, requester affidavit metadata, and be retrievable for e-discovery. SLA: delivery within 72 hours for MVP.

Mei (Infra): Storage implications: pinned objects cause retention exceptions. If we pin by flag we need per-org quotas and alerts. Archive export to cold store reduces load but adds cost. We can leverage object immutability where cloud provider supports it.

Jordan (SRE): Operational controls: RBAC for who can create/remove holds; emergency escalation flow where legal/senior sec can request forced hold; logs for every action. Also need metrics: pinned_bytes, pinned_count by tenant.

Priya (PM): Propose MVP scope (Q2):
- HTTP API to create/remove "evidence_hold" objects scoped to tenant
- RBAC enforcement + audit log entries for all hold actions
- Export endpoint that bundles relevant log segments + manifest (manifest = list of segment ids, checksums, created_by, timestamp, signature)
- Retention worker honors hold flag (skips GC)
- Quota enforcement UI + alerting
- Acceptance: legal can request export and receive bundle within 72h, manifest present, and audit trail shows requester identity

Evan (Eng): API sketch:
POST /v1/orgs/:org/holds
body: { "reason": "litigation-2026-03", "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z" }
POST /v1/orgs/:org/holds/:id/exports
GET /v1/orgs/:org/holds/:id/status

Manifest sample (conceptual):
{ "hold_id": "h-20260321-02", "segments": [{"id": "seg-123","sha256": "..."}], "created_by": "priya@redwood", "created_at": "2026-03-21T15:02:00Z", "signature": "sig-..." }

Nina (Security): BYOK interplay: docs must state that if customer-managed keys are rotated/deleted, export availability depends on key policy. For BYOK we should require a key-usage ACL that allows exports or a documented escrow process. That escrow flow is higher effort and can be Q3.

Carlos (Legal): Add acceptance test: create hold -> attempt normal retention purge -> verify retention skipped -> request export -> verify manifest and checksum match -> verify access controls on download.

Mei (Infra): Cost mitigation: default holds expire after 1 year unless extended; customers can request extensions via support. We'll implement soft quota defaults (e.g., 100GB pinned) and surcharge beyond.

Jordan (SRE): Runbook stub:
- How to apply emergency hold (roles + contact)
- How to verify integrity (checksums + signature verification)
- Revoke procedure and audit requirements

Priya (PM): Prioritization ask: customers A and B indicated SOC2 audit is blocked until they can demonstrate evidence retention. Recommend move to P1 for Q2 MVP without BYOK escrow. Escrow and HSM audit integration as P2 (Q3).

Evan (Eng): I'll scope implementation tasks and post an estimate by EOD Friday. Will prototype manifest signing code and retention-daemon change.

Nina (Security): I'll draft the security checklist for export bundles and the BYOK guidance note.

Carlos (Legal): I'll prepare the e-discovery acceptance language and sample affidavit fields.

Mei (Infra): I'll run cost model and quota parameters, share numbers in #product next week.

hold-bot: Hold h-20260321-02 created for org-acme by priya@redwood :lock:

Priya (PM): Thanks all. I'll open a PRD with these acceptance criteria and tag the owners.
